quandoUsar: Above a table or list, to show active filters as removable chips and clear them all at once.
When the user adds filters by choosing the field first and then the value, without leaving the bar (`addFilter`).
Collections with a few filter fields and one value per field: the added chip uses the field's `id`, so a new choice replaces the previous one.
quandoEvitar: Use `chip-group` when the options are few and can stay always visible as toggle chips.
Use `multi-select` when a single field needs several values; here each field holds only one.
Use `search-field` for free-text search; the menu here only offers predefined values.

teclado.acao: Open the “Add filter” menu with focus on the first field and, inside it, choose the focused item.
On the button, open the menu on the first or last item; inside the menu, move focus, wrapping at the ends.
Go to the first and last menu items; typing letters jumps to the item that starts with them.
`→` enters the values of the focused field; `←` goes back to the field list.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the button that opened it.
Moves through each chip's remove button and the bar's actions; leaving the open menu with `Tab` closes it.

acessibilidade: The bar is a `role="group"` named by `label`; each remove button has an `aria-label` with field and value, and a `role="status"` region announces filters added, changed, and removed.
When removing a chip by keyboard, focus moves to the neighboring chip or, if the list empties, to the “Add filter” button; when the menu closes, focus returns to that button.
The menu is a `role="dialog"` with `role="menu"` lists (`menuitemradio` on values) and a single `Tab` stop per list; the fixed texts (“Clear all”, “No filters applied”, “Remove…”) are in English.
movimento: Each chip opens and closes its own width space on a spring, so neighbors and actions slide along; a chip that moves to another line slides there, and the bar's height follows.

The “Add filter” button grows into the menu panel (width, height, and position on the same spring) and returns faster on close; the field and value steps slide in following the direction of navigation.
With “reduced motion”, chips, panel, and steps swap instantly or with a short fade.
responsivo: On screens up to 520 px the bar becomes a column, with chips on top and actions below, right-aligned; chips always wrap and long labels are truncated.
The menu panel opens upward when there's no room below, shifts to fit the window or the ancestor that clips content, and scrolls internally above `min(20rem, 55vh)`.
desempenho: Line wraps are animated by size observers on each chip and a `MutationObserver` on the list, and only in the 0.9 s following a filter change; resizing the window animates nothing.
notasIA: It is fully controlled: keep `filters` in state and update it in `onRemove`, `onClearAll`, and `addFilter.onAdd`; in `onAdd`, replace the chip with the same `id`, which is the field's `id`.
The chip received in `onAdd` carries in `value` the option's displayed text (its `label`), not its `value`; always pass `onClearAll`, because the “Clear all” button appears even without it.
The panel doesn't use a portal: avoid `overflow: hidden` on ancestors; `children` goes between the add button and “Clear all”, and `FilterMenu` is also exported for standalone use.
